card.name: Respiratory depression and overdose wording
card.fires_on: The word "respiratory" (or the start of respiration or overdose, e.g. "Over" + "d") in opioid and benzodiazepine warnings, just before "depression" or "ose".

modes.label: Respiratory before depression
modes.description: The word "respiratory" right before "depression" in opioid or benzodiazepine risk statements.
modes.example: The concomitant use of benzodiazepines and opioids increases the risk of<< respiratory>> depression because of actions at different receptor sites

modes.label: Inside overdose
modes.description: The "d" partway through "Overdose" in opioid risk headings.
modes.example: 5.11 Risk of Over<<d>>ose in Opioid Naïve

modes.label: Respiration in depressant warnings
modes.description: The word "respiration" after drugs that depress it.
modes.example: given concomitantly with other drugs that depress res<<piration>> [see WARNINGS ]

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about bodily danger and body effects such as danger, heat and body temperature, though the output effect is weak.
card.plain: It lights up on breathing-suppression and overdose terms in opioid warning text.
